questions.question: should I treat my boots out of box ? Annnnd how often should I treat them ?

hybrid.answer:
Everything he says here is about Blundstones, so how much applies to your boots depends on the leather.

**Out of the box**
- **Finished, oiled leather:** He reads Blundstone's FAQ saying most styles come pretreated, and that Blundstone doesn't recommend treating them out of the box [1]. Those are Blundstone's words, not his own advice.
- **Rustic Brown, Crazy Horse or rustic black:** The same FAQ says these distressed leathers don't carry the same pretreatment as finished, oiled leather [2]. For these he says he recommends conditioning, and he doesn't recommend leaving them dry [3].
- **Change of mind:** In his first review he assumed his distressed pair was treated and water resistant. He corrected that in his follow-up video after reading the FAQ [4].

**How often**
- **Newest view (2022):** He has no fixed schedule and treats his boots when he feels they need it. He says he probably does too little, and that others are more regimented [5].
- **Signs it's time:** The leather looks or feels dry, or water no longer beads on top. Dry-looking leather needs oil, and a lack of beading means more wax. He also says to clean boots regularly, since dirt wears leather down faster [6].
- **Earlier guidance (2019):** If you want the water resistance to last, expect to treat them every month, or maybe every week if you're very hard on them [7]. He also says to condition any leather you haven't treated in a few months [3].

**Order of steps (2022):** clean, then condition, then wax [8].

He hasn't covered out-of-box treatment for other boot types in the videos available here.

questions.question: So if I buy the levis 501 shrink to fit will they get tighter after washing?

hybrid.answer:
**Yes, the first time they get wet, mainly in the waist. Then they loosen again as you wear them.** The videos available here only cover that first soak or wash, not repeated washing afterward.

**Shrinking**
- He calls the 501 STF "shrink to fit." You put it in the bathtub and it shrinks, and he says you should usually go two sizes up [1].
- In his 2019 test, the jeans shrank mostly in the waist, and he says they "definitely did slim up" [2]. The length barely changed [2].

**Loosening**
- A week later in 2019, the upper thigh and waist had "definitely stretched" and he could wear a belt [3].
- In 2023 he guessed that frequent wear would stretch them out to about the same size as rinsed 501s [4].

**How you wash matters**
- In 2023 he says that if you put them in the dryer, they'd be a lot smaller from the start [5].
- His advice is not to toss them in the dryer or rinse them in very hot water, and then you get a really nice fit [6].

**Sizing**
- In 2021 he repeats Levi's advice: size up two in the waist and two inches in length. Followed that way, the pants fit regularly after you get them wet [7][8].
- He says that if you try them on before wetting them, they'll be too big [9].

questions.question: I'm usually a 33x30 in Levi's 502s, what size should I buy in these? [501 STF]

hybrid.answer:
Applying his rule to your numbers, he would point you to roughly a **35x32** in the 501 STF. That is two inches up in the waist and two inches up in the length from your usual 33x30.

**His rule (most recent first):**
- In 2025 he says of the STF: "You should usually go two sizes up." [1]
- In 2023 he sized up two on his own STFs (a 32 where his rinsed pair was a 30) [2]. He explains that you size up two in Levi's because the jeans shrink down [2].
- In 2021 he says Levi's advice is right: size up two in the waist and two inches longer. His example is that a 34 wearer should get a 36, though he doesn't think a 36 exists [3]. He says that after the soak the pants "will fit regularly" [3].

**Length:** On his own pair, he says he would definitely have gotten a 32 in length. He cuffed them anyway because of his style [4]. That matches the two-inches-longer rule.

**Waist caveat:** In 2019 he ignored Levi's advice and bought a 29 waist. He later said he could barely pull them on and couldn't breathe at first [5]. He also said he was glad he went small, because the waist now fits well [5]. His later, repeated advice is still to size up two [1][3].

**Not covered:** He hasn't said how Levi's 502 sizing compares to 501 STF sizing, so applying his rule to your 502 size is an assumption. He also hasn't said what to do if the exact size you need doesn't exist. He only notes that a 36 may not exist in his own example [3].

questions.question: Why do you cuff your jeans?

hybrid.answer:
He cuffs mainly for fit and style. In his 2020 one-year Levi's 501 update, he says he'd have bought a 32 length but cuffed them anyway, because he doesn't think his current style suits wider-legged pants left uncuffed [1].

In his 2019 Levi's 501 STF video, he says length is the most important thing for him. If jeans look too long, he thinks they just look bad. He also says the cuff can't be too thick [2]. In that video, the cuffed 501s looked a little better to him than uncuffed, though still wider than he likes [2].

His habit has shifted a bit when he wears boots. In his L.L.Bean boots video (Nov 2019), he says he used to always cuff his jeans but now likes them worn over his boots more. He says that calms the boots down as a loud fashion statement [3].

questions.question: So do you prefer [the Red Wing 3335s] over the 1907s?

hybrid.answer:
Yes, in the 2022 video he says he prefers the 3335s. He calls them his favorite boots he's ever had and says they beat his Blundstones, the 1907s and the 875s [1]. His reasoning is that the 1907s and 875s are heritage work boots, and he's "not really doing heritage works", he's hiking and walking in the woods. He says the 1907s and 875s are more beefily constructed, so someone who needs a tough boot probably shouldn't go for the 3335s. For all-around use, though, he calls the 3335s dramatically better [1]. He also likes their Vibram honey wheat mini lug sole, which he thinks won't break down as fast as the crepe soles on the 875s and 1907s [2].

Some nuance:
- He doesn't think the 3335s are necessarily better than Goodyear-welted boots in terms of construction. Their single stitch means they aren't some infinitely better level than the 1907s or 875s [3].
- In his 2021 video he made a value argument for the 1907 over the 875: for about $10 more you get a storm welt, a leather footbed and leather laces [4]. That was before the 3335 video.

Most recent view (September 2023): while culling his boot collection, he says he's on record calling the 3335s his favorite Red Wings, and "they still might be." But he says the 875s, 1907s and Iron Rangers each have characteristics he really likes. He likes the 3335s for their stitch-down construction, lighter weight and nimbleness, and says they're easier for walking or a light hike. He was selling them in that video [5].

questions.question: How do you feel bout blunnies as of Late 2023?

hybrid.answer:
As of his most recent video on the topic (September 2023), The Iron Snail is still a big fan of Blundstones, even though he's retiring his own pair.

- **Still positive:** About his heavily worn 585s, he says they've held up through everything and stayed probably his most water resistant boots. He calls Blundstones "just incredible," says he's a big fan and has always loved them, and notes some people really don't like them [1].
- **Retiring them anyway:** He says it's time to retire that pair. This is part of a cull of his boot collection because his girlfriend is moving into his small apartment, not a verdict against the boot [2]. He is also letting go of his heavy-duty Blundstone Extreme boots, which he'd thought were waterproof but are very water-resistant nubuck [3].

**How his view developed**
- **2019:** He called them by far his favourites of the three or four boots he had at the time, and recommended them if you'll keep them treated [4]. His main gripe was that the cemented soles can't technically be replaced [5].
- **2020 (one year in):** They looked great, performing as he'd hoped for the price. He said they're decent but not incredible as work boots, and that he'd pick a smoother leather over the rustic nubuck if he did it again [6][7].
- **2022:** He said he thinks they're worth the hype, though they're not as repairable as Goodyear-welted boots like Red Wings or Wolverines, and they're still some of his favourites [8].

He hasn't said anything on Blundstones after September 2023 in the videos available here.

questions.question: How does the made in England boot stack up to Solovairs? [Dr. Martens]

hybrid.answer:
He favors Solovair over the Made in England Dr. Martens, at least on pure value. The one exception is if you need the yellow stitching or the Dr. Martens name.

**His comparison (2022 video):**
- Solovair boots are cheaper than Made in England Docs. [1]
- He says the Made in England leather and midsoles are probably on par with Solovair. [1]
- Solovair is a much smaller company, and he says it is one of the original makers of the original Dr. Martens. [1]
- Solovairs have a shank, so he says they are more comfortable over long periods. Dr. Martens have none. He adds that Docs are easier to break in, while Solovairs are tougher at first but more comfortable down the line. [2][3]
- Solovairs are Goodyear welted in a more regularly accepted way, so they are easier to resole. [4]
- His Solovair derby eight-eye is essentially the same boot as Doc Martens, with cheaper prices, better quality and better features. [4]
- Solovair doesn't do the yellow stitching. If that matters to you, he says you have to get the Made in England Docs for the highest quality. Otherwise he suggests Solovair. [4]

**Caveat:** He loves Solovair but had problems with his own pair. After eight wears a back tab ripped off and a lace snapped. He assumed it was a manufacturing defect and had contacted them about it. [5]

**His later view on Made in England (2023 video):**
- He doesn't think the roughly $90 premium over the Thailand pair is objectively worth it. [6]
- The Made in England boots are for big Dr. Martens fans who want something made the way the old ones were. [7]
- He doesn't compare them to Solovair in that video.

**Bottom line:** If you want the best-built boot for the money, he points to Solovair. If you are a Dr. Martens devotee, the Made in England pair is the one he says to get.

questions.question: Hi, I am going on a 4 day hike and I am wondering if I can use my blundstone for them, what do you think?

hybrid.answer:
He hasn't covered multi-day hikes, but what he says suggests Blundstones are fine for casual hiking and not ideal for demanding terrain.

**Most recent view (2020, after a year of wear):**
- He took his Blundstones on hikes and up and down mountains in Maine. They got a little scuffed but "held up well" [1].
- He says they are "not good boots for mountaining apparently because they don't have uh good ankle support" [2]. That is the main caution for a 4-day hike, especially on rough or steep ground.
- The elastic side panels were still holding, if a bit looser than new [3].
- In his pond test he concluded they are fine if you're crossing a brook or stream or standing in some mud [4]. He wouldn't stand in still water in them [4].

**Earlier (2019, first review):**
- Walking through woods and all day around a city in brand-new Blundstones gave him no blisters [5]. He also says his girlfriend's untreated pair has been on hikes and snowshoeing and still looks new [6].
- For wet conditions he says to buy them knowing you'll have to take care of them, because their water resistance comes from treatment that you need to keep up [7]. His own pair was the distressed rustic brown style, which isn't pretreated like other Blundstones [8].

**Bottom line:** based on his comments, they can work for easy-to-moderate hiking, but the lack of ankle support is the drawback he names for mountain hiking. He also keeps separate boots for hiking, including Keens, which he calls hiking boots [9]. If your route is rough, a proper hiking boot is the safer pick. He hasn't said anything about carrying a pack or covering several days of mileage in them.

questions.question: I'm 5'11-225 lbs with a dad bod. What's the most cost efficient and quality t shirt for me? Also, what size would u prefer?

hybrid.answer:
**Short answer:** for your build, The Iron Snail's most recent advice points to **Muji** as the value pick. He hasn't given a specific size for someone 5'11" and 225 lbs.

**Why Muji (newest view, Sept 2025):** He calls the $20 Uniqlo tee probably the best t-shirt for the price, bar none [1]. But he says that if you're taller or wider in any way, you'd want Muji [2]. It costs about $4 or $5 more and is significantly longer and a good deal wider [3]. He adds that it tents out slightly, so you'd probably like it if you're a little bigger [3]. In June 2025 he said Muji's roughly $10 premium over Uniqlo feels justified, because the shirt feels better [4].

**Other options he rates well on value:**
- **House of Blanks ($35):** he calls it an outstanding value, made in Canada with combed ringspun cotton [5].
- **Los Angeles Apparel:** he says the one he tried runs very large, and that sizing down one might make it a winner [6].
- **Kirkland six-pack (~$4.20 each):** it's quite long, and he can't recommend it enough for a shirt under $5 or $6 [7]. That was his 2024 take, and he hasn't mentioned it in his newer value picks.

**Size:** he hasn't covered what size to buy at your height and weight. What he did say is to go with the longer, wider Muji if you're bigger [2][3], and that LA Apparel runs large enough that he'd size down [6]. Beyond that, check each brand's size chart yourself.

questions.question: Am I the only one who loves these videos but in the end still has no idea which to buy? Please just tell me: buy this one, or these 3. I can't decide between 25 options. [t-shirts]

hybrid.answer:
You're not alone, and he says as much. He doesn't name one best t-shirt. In his newest video (Sept 2025) he says the best shirt "just has to line up with your preferences" [1]. He also says he nearly couldn't publish it because so many brands now make a really good tee [1]. Instead he gives a favorite in each category, so his picks depend on what you want.

**If you want a short list, here are three based on his newest picks:**

1. **Uniqlo ($20), the cheap starter.** He says it's probably the best t-shirt you can get for the price [2]. In June 2025 he repeated that the price-to-quality ratio is insane [3]. If you're taller or wider, he points to Muji, which is slightly pricier but longer and wider [4].
2. **J. Press x American Trench, the all-arounder.** He's torn between this and the 3Sixteen, but says he'd probably pick J. Press for its rougher hand feel [5]. Choose 3Sixteen instead if you want perfectly smooth fabric with no twisting.
3. **Front General Store (about $40, made in Japan), the value pick with character.** He's leaning toward it today, and says House of Blanks is the pick if you want perfectly smooth fabric with no torque [6].

**His other category winners:**
- Wonder Looper, for Japan-style tees, because of its more universal fit [7].
- American Giant Everest, for heavyweights. It's lighter and fits more universally [7].
- Merz b. Schwanen 2M15, for the minimalist "Supremes" [8].

**Other things he's said:**
- Bronson wasn't in the Sept 2025 video, but he says it usually wins or comes close in t-shirt comparisons [9]. In June 2025 he said he'd probably give the win to Bronson's standard loopwheel tubular tee over Bravestar [10].
- Asket was his overall winner in July 2024 [11]. In 2025 he says it's still very high up but was left off the final list because that list is for shirts under $50 [12].

The three picks are my shortlist built from his stated favorites. He doesn't give a single "buy this one" himself.

questions.question: 1907 vs the 875's? What's the difference?

hybrid.answer:
In his view the 1907 is the better buy over the 875, mainly because of the storm welt and what comes bundled in.

**His case for the 1907 (2021 video)**
- The 1907 costs about $10 more than the 875, but he argues it isn't really more expensive. [1]
- It comes with Red Wing's inner leather footbed, which he says typically sells separately for $40. It can also be pulled out at the end of the day so the boots dry faster. [2]
- It has the storm welt, which he calls "invaluable." [2]
- It comes with leather laces, typically $15 on their own. He tallies the freebies as $55, then corrects it to technically $45 since you paid an extra $10. [2]
- Overall, he says it just seems like a better deal. [3]
- The 875 uses a Goodyear welt, per the video's summary of construction. [4]

**Soles:** In a later video he mentions the 875s and 1907s both have crepe soles, which he doesn't think hold up as long as the Vibram mini lug on the 3335. [5]

**Toughness:** In 2022 he describes the 1907s and 875s as the more beefily constructed boots, so they suit you better if you need a tough boot. [6]

**Not covered:** In the available videos he doesn't give a fit difference between the two. Each of the two is listed as having its own characteristics he likes, but he doesn't detail them side by side beyond the points above. [7]

questions.question: How does Uniqlo compare to The Front General Store,  Proclub, and Hanes? ie what is the best budget shirt?

hybrid.answer:
**Short answer:** Uniqlo is his pick for best budget t-shirt, with the Front General Store as the upgrade if you'll spend about $40. He sees Hanes as a cheap, soft basic and Pro Club as a rough, old-school shirt. His most recent word (Sept 2025) is that Uniqlo at $20 is "probably the best t-shirt that you can get bar none for the price" [1]. He calls it a rough, open-end "starter t-shirt" and says taller or wider guys should get Muji instead [2].

**Uniqlo**
- In June 2025 he said the $15 shirt has a bound collar and that the price-to-quality ratio is so good "You could end the video here" [3].
- In 2024 he called it the shirt that "may be" the best bargain, a heavyweight, coarse-feeling tee with a bound ribbed collar [4].

**Front General Store**
- It costs about $38–40 and is made in Japan. In 2025 he praised its "Great proportions, great feel" [5], and he still called it a really good shirt in June 2025 [6].
- In 2024 he put it among the best shirts you can get if you don't want to spend over $40. He gave it softness 6/10 and zero length shrinkage because it's pre-washed [7].
- It's a step up in price from Uniqlo, not a budget replacement.

**Hanes**
- In 2024 he called it "your classic $10 great shirt". He gave it softness 7/10 and much softer than Pro Club, but it shrank 6.73% in length [8].
- In June 2025 he grouped the huge mass-market brands, including Hanes, as very cheap shirts that are rushed through production. Of the five he had from those brands, all had a defect [9]. He still feels Uniqlo is the better value than these [3].

**Pro Club**
- In 2024 he said he liked everything about it. It's an old-school American shirt, and he's confident it uses open-end yarns. He called it the roughest shirt on that list (softness 4/10, 6.86% length shrink) [10].
- He hasn't compared it with Uniqlo in later videos.

**Bottom line:** Uniqlo wins on value, Front General Store is the nicer shirt for roughly double the price, Hanes is a soft $10 basic with defect and shrink caveats, and Pro Club is the roughest of the four. He didn't directly rank Uniqlo against Pro Club or Hanes in a single head-to-head.

questions.question: Would you recommend this or the flint and tinder for someone who would use it like a rain jacket but also a windbreaker and a spring light jacket?

hybrid.answer:
I'm assuming "this" is the Barbour. If so, The Iron Snail's reasoning points to the **Barbour for the rain and wind side**, while the **Flint and Tinder is the easier, more comfortable everyday light jacket**. He hasn't compared the two directly or tested the Flint and Tinder in rain, so this is his stated points applied to your use.

**Barbour (most recent view, 2025)**
- He calls it the lightest fabric in his ranking: "6 oz silk oil." [1] He says it isn't a designated rain jacket, but it works any time of year, including spring. [2][3]
- Rain features he likes: storm cuffs that help in bad weather [4], plus a storm flap over the zipper [5]. In 2021 he also recommended getting the hood. [6]
- On water: in his shower test a freshly waxed jacket didn't leak. He says it's not waterproof but is very water-resistant when properly treated. [7] The catch is that as the wax wears and the patina develops, you lose some practicality. [8]
- On wind, he said thornproof-finish Barbours add wind and water resistance because of the tighter weave. [9] He didn't say which finish his own jacket has.

**Flint and Tinder waxed trucker**
- He says it's for everyone. [10] It's lighter weight but not crazy lightweight, so it's comfortable. [11]
- It's lined, so you don't get wax on your skin, and he thinks $300 for a lined, US-made waxed jacket is hard not to recommend. [12] This was a sponsored segment from Huckberry, though he says he'd praised the jacket many times before the sponsorship. [13]
- In 2023 he described the Huckberry waxed trucker as the lightest jacket in that comparison and said it suits warmer weather because it has no lining. [14] In 2025 he calls the Flint and Tinder lined, so the two descriptions differ.
- He hasn't said how it handles rain or wind.

**Bottom line:** for a jacket that has to double as a rain shell and windbreaker, the Barbour is the one he's described with real rain features. The Flint and Tinder fits the light spring-jacket role, but he hasn't addressed its weather protection.

**What he hasn't said:** In the videos available here he doesn't mention a flannel-lined version. He also doesn't say whether the lined jacket is a changed or different version of the unlined one he criticized in 2023.
